cards.title: 2.1.1 Temperature and the Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics
body: Thermodynamics is the area of physics concerned with the relationship between heat and work.
The laws of thermodynamics describe what happens as energy is transformed into work or work is transformed into energy.
Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of an object.
The temperature of an object is a measure of how hot or cold the object is.

cards.title: 2.1.2 Temperature Scales
body: A thermometer is a device that measures temperature.
The operation of a thermometer depends on some physical property that changes continuously and regularly with change of temperature.
The thermometric property (temperature dependent property) most commonly used to measure temperature is thermal expansion.
Nearly all substances expand with increasing temperature and contract with decreasing temperature.

cards.title: 2.1.3 Thermometers
body: Thermometry is the science of temperature measurement.
Any material solid, liquid, or gas that expands uniformly over a certain temperature range can be used in a thermometer.
The thermometer is an instrument used for measuring the temperature of a body.
The operation of a thermometer is based on a measurable physical change which goes with a temperature change.

At this temperature, the heat added starts to change the state of water from liquid to steam or vapour.

body: Everything that is not part of the system is considered to be external to the system or, in other words, is the surroundings of the system.

glossary.meaning: Thermodynamics is the area of physics concerned with the relationship between heat and work.
Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of an object.
Thermal equilibrium is a situation in which two objects in thermal contact with each other cease to have a net exchange of energy.
Thermometric property is a physical property that changes continuously and regularly with change of temperature.
Heat is a transfer of energy due to temperature difference.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Two point charges, $$q_1$$ and $$q_2$$, are separated by distance $$r$$, experiencing an electrostatic force $$F$$. If the separation distance is reduced to $$r / 2$$ while the charges remain constant, what is the new electrostatic force?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Write Coulomb's Law equation**  
$$F_1 = k \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2}$$

**Step 2: Substitute the new distance $$r' = r / 2$$**  
$$F_2 = k \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{(r/2)^2} = k \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2 / 4}$$

**Step 3: Simplify the expression**  
$$F_2 = 4 \left( k \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2} \right) = 4 F_1$$

**Step 4: Final Result**  
The new force is **$$4 F$$**.
